articles.excerpt: Former American Airlines and FedEx pilot Matthew 'Whiz' Buckley discusses why a pressurization malfunction demands swift action and how crews identify an appropriate airport for an unscheduled landing...
articles.body_text:
Former American Airlines and FedEx pilot Matthew 'Whiz' Buckley discusses why a pressurization malfunction demands swift action and how crews identify an appropriate airport for an unscheduled landing.

An incoming flight to Hawaii prompted an emergency response after multiple crew members began feeling ill during the journey.

Seven Hawaiian Airlines flight attendants experienced nausea and headaches after an unknown odor was reported inside the cabin, according to reports.

The incident unfolded Sept. 24 aboard Alaska Airlines Flight 803, operated as Hawaiian Airlines between Los Angeles and Honolulu, Alaska Airlines told Fox News Digital.

CO-PILOT BECOMES SICK MIDAIR AS CREW ILLNESS REPORTS EMERGE AFTER OVERNIGHT LAYOVER

The Airbus A330, carrying 252 passengers and nine crew members, landed "without incident" at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu, according to the airline.

Upon arrival, seven flight attendants were evaluated and released by medical personnel. No passengers required medical attention, Alaska Airlines said.

An incoming flight to Hawaii prompted an emergency response after multiple crew members began feeling ill during the journey. (iStock)

"Safety is our priority, and we thank the medical professionals for their response," the airline said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

First responders from multiple city and state agencies had been waiting at the airport ahead of the flight's arrival around 12:30 p.m., according to local news outlet Hawaii News Now.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Paramedics and EMTs evaluated the affected flight attendants outside Terminal 1, and all seven declined transportation to an emergency room, the outlet reported.

The source of the odor has not been publicly identified.

Seven Hawaiian Airlines flight attendants experienced nausea and headaches after an unknown odor was reported inside the cabin. (iStock)

Following the incident, the aircraft was being inspected before returning to service, according to Hawaii News Now.

Fox News Digital previously reported on another flight disrupted after an unusual odor was detected onboard.

American Airlines Flight 719 was traveling from Rome to Philadelphia when it diverted to Dublin about three hours into the trip after an odor was reported inside the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner.

First responders from multiple city and state agencies had been waiting at the airport ahead of the flight's arrival (not pictured). (iStock)

American Airlines said the smell was traced to an onboard oven. Paramedics met the aircraft after it landed in Dublin, where several flight attendants and one passenger were reportedly evaluated and released.

The flight was carrying 281 passengers and 12 crew members. Affected travelers were provided hotel accommodations and continued to Philadelphia on alternate flights the following morning, according to the airline.

Fox News Digital's Bonny Chu contributed to this report.

Kelly McGreal is a production assistant with the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Bessent says Iran will have 'nothing left to trade' within two weeks as oil lifeline dries up
articles.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent discusses the state of the Iranian economy, strength and resilience of the U.S. economy and more on 'Sunday Morning Futures.' Bessent highlights wage increases, busine...
articles.body_text:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent discusses the state of the Iranian economy, strength and resilience of the U.S. economy and more on 'Sunday Morning Futures.' Bessent highlights wage increases, business growth and the impact of the administration's tax cuts on American families. He also analyzes trade negotiations with China, including a $30 billion tariff cut agreed upon by the nations.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted Sunday that Iran will complete its remaining oil shipments to China within two weeks, leaving Tehran with "nothing left to trade for anything" as the Trump administration intensifies its economic pressure campaign against the regime.

Bessent said only about 15 million barrels of Iranian oil remain out for delivery now that the U.S. is blockading the ports, describing the dwindling shipments as evidence that Operation Economic Outcast has left Tehran economically isolated.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent participates in a Shield of the Americas event during the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York on Sept. 22, 2026. (REUTERS)

"They will have nothing to trade for anything, probably within the next two weeks. They are going to make their final deliveries of oil to China, and then they will have nothing," he said.

MILLIONS OF BARRELS OF IRANIAN OIL SIT BEYOND TRUMP BLOCKADE AS HE VOWS ‘ZERO LEAKAGE’

The Treasury chief said he believed Iran was "feeling the pressure," leading to their renewed interest in striking a deal. President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's latest proposal on Saturday, telling Axios on Sunday that "they overplayed their hand."

Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of the port city of Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. (Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images)

"I expect more talks with Iran [this week]," Trump told the outlet during a phone interview. "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand."

IRAN ‘MISCALCULATING’ BY BETTING ON MIDTERMS AFTER 3-HOUR TALKS, TRUMP OFFICIALS WARN

Tehran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a highly trafficked waterway in the region that is critical to global oil shipping. Bessent said it's already open.

"We're averaging now 15 to 22 million barrels a day. It was at about 20 pre-conflict . . . So think of it this way, Larry," he said. "The score is the United States, one billion — more than one billion barrels have gotten out — Iran, zero."

The point of Operation Economic Outcast is to ensure that Iran adheres to the terms of a potential future deal, Bessent added.

"They are isolated from the world. They're a pariah state. And my job is to make sure that, when they come with a deal, that they want to stick to it. They did not stick to the MOU [Memorandum of Understanding]. And, next time, if there is a deal — that's at President Trump's discretion — that they will stick to it, because they are on their knees."

Fox News Digital's Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.

Max Bacall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital covering media, culture and comedy.

Sen. J...
articles.body_text:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-PA, triggered a wave of laughs at a speaking event on Saturday, Sept. 26, after mistakenly referring to himself as a "life-long Republican." (Texas Tribune via Facebook)

Sen. John Fetterman, D-PA, triggered a wave of laughs at a speaking event on Saturday after mistakenly referring to himself as a "lifelong Republican."

Fetterman made the statement while on stage at the Texas Tribune Festival, going on to quickly correct himself and assert that he has no reason to abandon the Democratic Party.

The moment came when an attendee at the event asked why Fetterman doesn't run as an independent.

MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH

Sen. John Fetterman, D-PA, triggered a wave of laughs at a speaking event on Saturday after mistakenly referring to himself as a "lifelong Republican." (Joseph A. Wulfsohn/Fox News Digital.)

"Because I’m a lifelong Republican," he said, realizing his mistake. "I guarantee you that will break through. That will get clipped."

Fetterman gave a keynote address earlier in the event where he elaborated on his criticisms of both the Republican and Democratic parties.

FETTERMAN WINS PRAISE FOR 'GUTS' AFTER GOING TOE-TO-TOE WITH JON STEWART OVER ISRAEL SUPPORT

"I don’t have a reason to," Fetterman said of joining Republicans. "But for a big-tent situation, it’s easier to be included in that big tent to say America deserved 9/11 or America is worse than Al-Qaida than being very proud to stand on the side of Israel."

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., leaves the Senate floor at the U.S. Capitol on July 15, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Fetterman admitted he believed he has "no path as a Republican," but acknowledged that many Democrats are frustrated by his willingness to work with the opposing party.

FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE'

"If the Democratic Party votes me out or expels me, they’re always entitled to do that," he said.

Fetterman has been welcomed with open arms by Republicans to join the party after he floated leaving his own caucus and spurred further speculation that he would jump ship after dropping a video introducing his colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention earlier this month.

FETTERMAN TEASES WHERE HIS TRUE LOYALTY LIES AFTER SURPRISE APPEARANCE AT GOP CONVENTION

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gifts Democratic Sen. John Fetterman a silver-plated pager, commemorating the operation that used pagers against Hamas leaders and operatives. Fetterman visited Israel to show his support in its fight against the terrorist group that attacked on Oct. 7, 2023, killing more than 1,200 and taking many hostages. (GPO)

But the progressive-turned-centrist has repeatedly affirmed his Democratic ties, even as the knives have come out to cut him loose from the Senate.

Fetterman started his career in the Senate after besting Dr. Mehmet Oz in a tight race for power in 2022, where he clinched a historically thin Democratic majority in 2022 running on a progressive platform.

But since then, he has become a thorn in Democrats’ side and challenged the direction of the party.

Earlier this year, Fetterman warned that if Democrats became more entrenched in anti-Israel policy positions, he would exit the party, and has taken jabs at the party’s direction during this midterm election cycle as far-left progressives, like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, have emerged as standard-bearers.

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.

Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

articles.title: Serbia’s populist president Aleksandar Vučić resigns to run for prime minister
articles.excerpt:
Vučić not allowed to seek third presidential term and election will test his grip on rule after widespread protests

Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to...
articles.body_text:
Vučić not allowed to seek third presidential term and election will test his grip on rule after widespread protests

Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to become the prime minister in an upcoming early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.

Vučić’s second presidential term would otherwise end in May next year. He is banned by the Serbian constitution from seeking a third term and said he was resigning to lead his rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) in the 25 October ballot.

The governing populists face a major challenge at the ballot from a youth-backed movement that led the protests triggered by a train station canopy collapse in November 2024 that killed 16 people in the northern city of Novi Sad.

University students demanded accountability for the tragedy. Their struggle for justice and against corruption has grown into a strong movement that will attempt to oust Vučić’s government after 14 years in power. Vučić has been either prime minister or president for the past 12 years.

“I am resigning the duty of the president of the republic,” Vučić said, reading the text of his resignation.

The ballot in October will be held against a backdrop of high political tensions as Vučić’s populists seek to remain in office despite widespread discontent. His decision to run for prime minister is seen both as an attempt to retain a top position, and to boost his party’s chances against the student movement.

In recent weeks Vučić has toured the country with live coverage on pro-government media. He has opened new roads, offered assistance money and cheaper medicines, and visited voters in their homes. More recently, he was filmed driving in his brother’s car to some of the events.

The prime minister in Serbia is formally more powerful than the president. But Vučić still took a dominant role during his two five-year terms, sometimes presiding over government sessions and routinely announcing all important decisions and plans.

Serbia’s independent Bureau for Social Research has filed a complaint alleging that Vučić has abused a public institution as president to promote his party, which he has dismissed. There has been no response from the anti-corruption authorities that are under government control.

After Vučić’s resignation, the acting president will be a close ally and former prime minister, Ana Brnabić, who is the outgoing speaker of Serbia’s 250-member parliament. After a new parliament is elected in the 25 October ballot, the new speaker will take over from Brnabić, appoint the prime minister and schedule a presidential vote.

Vučić and his party have been accused of rampant corruption, organised crime links and a clampdown on democratic freedoms, including the critical media. The SNS have gradually taken control of all state institutions since coming to power in 2012, while denying abuse of office and repeatedly pledging to fight graft.

The student-backed election list includes little-known experts, professors, teachers, athletes and other individuals from all walks of life. Groups of students have been touring the country on bicycles as part of their campaign urging the rule of law and an end to corruption.

Analysts say the student group and Vučić are polling closely, heralding a tight race and a referendum-like atmosphere. Also running are Vučić’s allies, the Socialist party, a pro-EU opposition alliance and several smaller groups.

Authorities have pushed hard against protesters with police violence and detentions, as Vučić, without offering evidence, accused his opponents and critical media of an intention to “destroy the state” under unspecified foreign influence.

He told Serbia’s state RTS Television earlier on Sunday that foreign powers and unidentified people in the country planned to stir unrest on election night.

Serbia’s efforts to join the EU have stalled under Vučić because of democratic backsliding and a refusal to join sanctions against Russia over the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Fetterman claims Democratic ‘big tent’ has more room for ‘America deserved 9/11’ than Israel support
articles.excerpt: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., told CBS News’ Major Garrett at the Texas Tribune Festival that Democrats’ "big tent" had increasingly made room for anti-Israel voices and pointed to Hasan Piker’s large A...
articles.body_text:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., told CBS News’ Major Garrett at the Texas Tribune Festival that Democrats’ "big tent" had increasingly made room for anti-Israel voices and pointed to Hasan Piker’s large Austin crowd as evidence.

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., claimed on Saturday that the Democratic Party’s "big tent" had become more accommodating of people who say America "deserved 9/11" than Democrats who strongly support Israel, as the Pennsylvania senator explained why the issue has increasingly put him at odds with parts of his party.

Fetterman made the comparison at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin while CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett asked whether there were any circumstances under which he would leave the Democratic Party.

"It’s easier to be included in that big tent to say ‘America deserved 9/11’ or America is ‘worse than Al-Qaeda’ than being very proud to stand on the side of Israel," Fetterman said. "More and more members of my caucus are becoming more and more anti-Israel."

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., said the Democratic Party’s "big tent" had become more accommodating to people who say America "deserved 9/11" than to Democrats who strongly support Israel. (Fox News Digital)

SEN JOHN FETTERMAN PLEDGES TO BE 'LAST MAN STANDING' IN THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN SUPPORT OF ISRAEL

Fetterman saying America "deserved 9/11" was a reference to streamer Hasan Piker, who made the remark during a 2019 livestream before later saying he "obviously" did not believe Americans deserved the terrorist attacks. Fetterman pointed to the interest in Piker's appearances as evidence of where he believed political enthusiasm was building on the left.

"I’m just describing that’s where a lot of the energy on the left is in my party," Fetterman said.

The tension comes as Democratic voters’ attitudes toward Israel have shifted sharply.

A Pew Research Center survey conducted in March found 80% of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents held an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 53% in 2022. Overall, 60% of American adults viewed Israel unfavorably.

Fetterman warned that "more and more" members of the Democratic caucus were becoming anti-Israel and pointed to Senate votes on Israeli military assistance as evidence of the shift. (Fox News Digital)

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

"80% Democrats have a negative view on Israel," Fetterman said. "If America stops supporting Israel or turns their back on Israel, that must mean that we don't even believe in ourselves anymore. I mean that's that's our special ally and that is the kinds of values and the kinds of the you know how we live here that's that only exists in one place in that region and that's that's Israel."

"If our party ever becomes, and just makes it official, the anti-Israel party, that’s when I would leave, because that’s been a moral clarity for me," Fetterman said.

Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin addressed that tension in comments to Fox News Digital on Monday, defending Democrats as a "big tent" party while distancing the DNC from Piker.

Fetterman said support for Israel could ultimately become a red line for his Democratic Party membership if the party formally became "anti-Israel." (GPO)

DEMOCRATS CONDEMNING HASAN PIKER AS BACKLASH SPREADS THROUGH PARTY

"Let me just say that I think it’s absolutely disgusting and deplorable the things that Hasan Piker has said," Martin said. "But he does not represent the Democratic Party, and he certainly doesn’t represent the viewpoints of almost every one of our candidates and our elected officials."

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Fetterman also referenced resolutions introduced by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., while discussing Democratic opposition to Israeli military assistance.

In April, 40 Senate Democrats voted to block a $295 million sale of bulldozers to Israel and 36 supported blocking a $151.8 million sale of 1,000-pound bombs.

Those resolutions did not concern Iron Dome funding, which Fetterman separately cited Saturday as an example of defensive assistance to Israel.

CJ joined Fox News Digital's team in 2026, which highlights the vital role journalism plays in shaping politics and culture. He has years of experience analyzing and reporting on the news media.

CJ graduated from Long Beach State University in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a minor in Journalism.

articles.title: Andy Burnham to fight next election with plan for NHS-style care service
articles.excerpt:
PM says he is willing to expend political capital to bring in universal service that would be funded by ‘everybody’

Analysis: can Labour hang on to Burnham bounce?

Andy Burnham will fight the next e...
articles.body_text:
PM says he is willing to expend political capital to bring in universal service that would be funded by ‘everybody’

Analysis: can Labour hang on to Burnham bounce?

Andy Burnham will fight the next election with a pledge to finally fix the broken social care system, acknowledging that he is willing to expend political capital by asking taxpayers to cover the cost.

As Labour’s party conference began in Liverpool, he pledged to “rip the plaster off” to radically transform care, setting out a vision for a universal service that would be free at the point of use for everybody in England.

The prime minister said the new NHS-style service would be funded by “everybody” but did not give further details of how his long-term plan would be paid for, indicating that a tax rise may be on the cards.

He said Labour would put the proposals into its next general election manifesto so that voters could give their endorsement, in the hope of reducing the risk that political attacks over “death taxes” would sink the policy.

Burnham acknowledged there were risks in a nationwide reform, likely to be costly and complicated to implement, although he rejected suggestions it could cost £18bn a year. “It’s not that high,” he told the BBC.

“Somebody needs to grasp the nettle. I will be the one to do that,” he said. “I realise it might require me to spend some political capital, that it might make me unpopular with some, but that isn’t going to stop [me].”

But he said he would take his time to work out how it could be fairly funded. “The challenge in the public finances is real. So it has to be done carefully, without putting extra strain on the public purse. But I will bring forward proposals.”

Labour’s annual gathering is intended to be an upbeat affair, with the prime minister wanting to restore hope that some of the country’s most intractable political problems can be solved despite severe economic headwinds.

With political courage a theme of the conference, he said in an interview with the Guardian at the weekend: “There’s always things you can do, it’s just whether you’re prepared to do them.”

Burnham acknowledged the public finances were “challenging” ahead of next month’s budget but he said delivering fiscal stability would be “crucial”, because only then would the government be able to focus on fixing bigger problems.

A series of global economic shocks, including the Iran conflict, has put the UK economy under intense inflationary pressure and pushed up borrowing costs, leaving the government with limited room for manoeuvre.

On Sunday, Burnham said he did not want to focus on a “narrative of doom” about the UK’s economy but that he would show in his leader’s speech that he was prepared to take tough decisions.

He acknowledged there was “real concern” in the financial markets about the state of the British economy, pointing to the “febrile” state of the global backdrop. He said he was willing to cut government spending to balance the books, and he believed money could be saved by taking a more “productive” long-term approach to issues such as rough sleeping and youth unemployment.

Amid concerns that the government could be hemmed in at the budget by the parlous state of the public finances, he said the chancellor, John Healey, would be “highly prudent” in running the economy. “I won’t do what the previous Tory government did and take risks with the economy that are actually still hurting us right now,” he said.

Burnham suggested to the Guardian that a significant fiscal buffer would be necessary, with speculation that the Treasury could now consider £15bn acceptable.

“I do think it is crucial to have stability and to show that there’s a willingness to face up to the reality of some of these difficult things,” he said. “But actually from that stability, the permission can come to make bigger change that, in the end, could put the country in a stronger position in relation to the public finances.”

Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, said the “heavy lifting” on making the case for rejoining the EU needed to be done by the government now, after Burnham signalled that the move could be in the next manifesto.

“The pitch rolling must be done now, explaining to the country the dis-benefits of being outside the European Union and the benefits of being part of this family,” Khan said.

However, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, appeared to criticise Khan – and Burnham – telling Politico that the speculation “frankly cause[s] a lot of uncertainty for business”.

Meanwhile, plans for a third runway at Heathrow are once again up in the air after Burnham refused to say whether he backed the “contested” project, which is delayed by up to four years, saying it was “principally” a matter for London.

articles.title: Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US
articles.excerpt:
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles

Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is be...
articles.body_text:
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles

Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.

The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices.

Images circulating on Sunday showed shirtless men being handcuffed in a dark country lane in the early hours of Sunday after police were called to reports of three suspicious vans travelling towards RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, which hosts US air force missions against Iran.

The suspected plot appears to have been foiled by chance when a member of the public spotted unusual behaviour late at night in the countryside from a group of men and called 999.

The major incident saw the residents of 85 households in the Cotswolds village of Whelford rapidly evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre and led to a 400m cordon being placed around the white vans as robots from the army’s bomb squad examined them.

Tests were ongoing to see if the suspected explosive devices were viable, with bomb robots deployed in the Gloucestershire countryside as investigations continued.

After their initial arrest over explosives offences, the five men detained early on Sunday were further arrested later in the day on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act. The pictures of the men with their shirts off could point to a precautionary measure against the risk of suicide vests or concealed weapons.

At least one van carried the logo of a fuel company and a phone number missing a digit. A real fuel company of the same name firmly rejected any connection to the incident and said: “We are extremely concerned that our company’s name has been used without our knowledge or permission.” It said it was cooperating with the authorities.

In a statement counter-terrorism police said: “At around 12.45am today (Sunday 27 September), police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the airbase.

“Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.”

The arrests come as the war between the US and Iran limps on. In July Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps noted RAF Fairford’s use by US bombers, warning the UK that “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces”.

Counter-terror police and the security services are searching for the motive. The circumstances of the arrest near the base and prior warnings from Tehran, leave an Iranian motive high in the investigators’ and government’s thinking. But sources warn nothing is being ruled out including a jihadist or other motive, and the UK threat level remains at severe, the second highest, meaning an attack is highly likely.

Whether there was any foreign involvement forms part of the investigation, and Iran’s ministry of intelligence and security has orchestrated attacks overseas before.

Any proven link with Iran would be a dramatic escalation in hostilities between the UK and Tehran. While several recent incidents in the UK have been linked to the Middle-Eastern country, including the antisemitic arson attack on four Hatzola ambulances in Golders Green, the alleged plot at RAF Fairford appears to be significantly more serious.

And it raises urgent questions for the UK security services after it appeared the authorities had been unaware of the alleged plot, with police only moving on the three vans after a 999 call from a local resident who spotted them as she drove home.

The US president, Donald Trump, claimed to have had the suspects under view for a “long time” and alleged the men “were looking to do big damage” – although the Guardian understands the operation was not intelligence-led, suggesting investigators had not known about any potential plot in advance.

“It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job,” Trump said.

The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, was being updated on the matter from Liverpool, where the Labour party conference is taking place. He cancelled plans to take part in a journalists versus politicians football match in order to take calls about the incident.

He said it was “deeply concerning” and the government will “always take every step necessary” to protect people.

Fairford has a particularly long runway, which extends almost 2 miles (3km). It is reinforced to support heavy bombers such as the B-1 and B-52, which have been deployed in attacks on Iran. The aircraft are capable of carrying large payloads, including “bunker buster” bombs.

In March this year, after then prime minister, Sir Keir Starmer, granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases, four American bombers landed at RAF Fairford and the US started using British bases for “specific defensive operations”.

There have been protests in recent months over the UK government’s decision to allow the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the strait of Hormuz.

At the time of Iran’s warning in July, a government spokesperson said: “Our armed forces are ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad. The UK stands ready 24/7 to defend itself.”

Evacuated residents of Whelford spoke of “heightened tensions” in recent weeks around the base with more frequent, visible police patrols.

Outside Cirencester leisure centre, Jason, a resident of Whelford who declined to give his surname, said: “There have been heightened tensions recently around the base, we are aware it is used by the USAF … It always feels pretty safe. Some residents have seen increased police patrols.”

It was unclear when people would be able to go back to their normal lives; those at the leisure centre said they had been asked by authorities if they had anywhere else to stay on Sunday night.

The Fairford youth football club, about 1.5 miles (2.4km) north-west of Whelford, was taken over as a temporary base for the emergency service response to the incident. There were several police vehicles, ambulances, fire engines, pop-up tents and a large mobile command-unit vehicle in the grounds.

Richard Ocone, the assistant chief constable with Gloucestershire constabulary, said: “We appreciate the disruption this will have caused and would like to reassure them we are working as quickly as we can to get them back in their properties.”

articles.title: At least 12 dead and dozens missing after a vessel capsizes in DRC
articles.excerpt:
A vessel carrying fish traders has capsized in Lake Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), killing at least 12 people with dozens still missing, authorities said.

The vessel was carr...
articles.body_text:
A vessel carrying fish traders has capsized in Lake Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), killing at least 12 people with dozens still missing, authorities said.

The vessel was carrying more than 50 people on Saturday night near Idjwi Island in South Kivu province, said Félix Habiragi, chief of the village of Kisheke near the scene.

He said the cause of the accident was not immediately clear and about 15 people were rescued.

The vessel was transporting fish traders and goods from Bwina on Idjwi Island to Boza, according to local administrator, Muhindo Ntambuka Pascal. Videos that appear to be from the scene showed villagers and other passengers pulling bodies from the lake.

Boat accidents are common in the DRC, as rivers and lakes are a major means of transport for over 100 million people. Vessels are often overloaded with goods and passengers, many of whom frequently travel without life jackets.

“The authorities had, in particular, begun requiring passengers to wear life jackets. Today, however, many people continue to travel without them,” said Dorcelle Bagazane, a civil society member in Idjwi.

Earlier this week, at least 41 people died and 49 were rescued when a boat capsized on Lake Tanganyika in the DRC. It was reportedly carrying about 100 people and cargo when it capsized near the Congolese village of Mapera.

articles.title: Forgetting names and losing keys may signal something other than dementia
articles.excerpt: Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerat...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerative disease.

Everyday memory lapses, like misplaced keys or forgotten names, are often overinterpreted as early signs of dementia, but neuroscience experts say actual early cognitive changes may be reversible if addressed promptly.

Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerative disease.

"For most people, it's just because you're stressed or you're tired and weren't paying attention," Wood told Fox News Digital at Strong New York, the city's largest annual fitness and wellness festival.

DOCTOR REVEALS '10-YEAR RULE' FOR EVALUATING BRAIN FOG AND DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS

"If you want to remember something ... you need to actually be focused, be paying attention. You need to tell your brain it's important to remember it."

Wood said memory formation works in three stages: encoding (forming a memory), consolidation (storing it) and retrieval (accessing it).

Cognitive changes during aging are not inevitable, and taking proactive lifestyle steps early can help maintain or even restore brain function. (iStock)

When someone is stressed or sleep-deprived, the issue is typically retrieval, he said — the memory exists in the brain, but the individual struggles to access it in the moment.

In contrast, people experiencing a neurodegenerative disease often fail to encode the memory in the first place.

‘MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON’ HERO SULLY SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER’S WARNING SIGNS HE MISSED YEARS AGO

"They don't even remember or notice that there's something going on," Wood said. "If you're noticing something's not quite right, that's usually a good sign."

Dementia is clinically defined as the loss of cognitive function that's severe enough to impair an individual's ability to manage daily life independently. Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia account for 70% to 90% of cases, with many individuals showing signs of both.

Research indicates that at least 50% of dementia cases can be prevented by modifying lifestyle and health risk factors.

True memory problems stem from a failure to encode new memories in the brain, whereas stress-related forgetfulness is merely an issue with retrieving existing memories. (iStock)

Key preventable risk factors include heart and metabolic health problems, as well as hearing and vision loss.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Wood emphasized that addressing physical health issues — such as obtaining hearing aids or undergoing cataract surgery — directly lessens cognitive decline risk.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"If you expect decline, you won't do the things that will prevent decline from happening," Wood told Fox News Digital. "Believing that it's possible means you'll actually engage in these processes, and then through that, you can prevent a lot of this decline."

Minor memory lapses, like forgetting keys or names, are usually caused by stress or fatigue rather than early dementia, the expert said. (iStock)

Wood's focus on reversible causes of cognitive symptoms aligns with guidance from Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic, which note that several treatable medical conditions can mimic early dementia symptoms or contribute to subjective cognitive decline.

Common reversible causes include the following.

Managing physical health issues — such as controlling high blood pressure, treating vision or hearing loss and staying physically active — directly reduces cognitive decline risks. (iStock)

Cleveland Clinic highlights that early clinical intervention is critical when individuals notice changes in "brain fog" or executive function.

"How your brain functions on a day-to-day basis is kind of the output of everything your brain is dealing with," said Wood. "But if you start to notice something, there's still time to make some changes if you need to."

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.body_text:
Will Ospreay spoke to reporters at the AEW Double or Nothing post-show scrum on May 24, 2026.

Will Ospreay was in The Death Riders’ dojo for months trying to hone the visceral side of his pro wrestling athleticism in hopes of winning the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) World Championship. He built a strange relationship with Jon Moxley in the meantime but failed to earn the respect of the rest of the faction.

Ospreay and The Death Riders split up ahead of the Brit’s AEW World Championship match against Kenny Omega at All In. However, it was Moxley who handed Ospreay the Union Jack before he entered Wembley Stadium and later defeated Omega to win the title.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Will Ospreay hits Jon Moxley with a thrust kick at AEW All Out on Sept. 26, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

The odd couple type of relationship flashed again after All In. AEW owner Tony Khan made Moxley the first opponent for Ospreay. It all culminated into the brawl at All Out.

Ospreay appeared to completely sever ties with The Death Riders when he lit their flag on fire before the match. Moments later, the fight began.

Moxley, with his slow and methodical pace, tried to inflict maximum damage. He nailed a DDT on Ospreay from the top turnbuckle. He worked on Ospreay’s neck from here, nailing a piledriver on the champion in the middle of the ring. When Ospreay tried a springboard cutter, Moxley countered that as well.

Moxley had Ospreay’s number, but he didn’t have Ospreay’s heart. A quick reversal led to a powerbomb and pin attempt. Ospreay hit Moxley with a Hidden Blade but with the referee down, the rest of The Death Riders jumped into the match to give Moxley an advantage.

Jon Moxley hits Will Ospreay with a piledriver at AEW All Out on Sept. 26, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Luckily, Ospreay had backup. Andrade El Idolo and "Speedball" Mike Bailey backed up Ospreay to even the odds. Alex Windsor, fresh off a Chicago street fight, came out to take care of Marina Shafir.

Moxley came to his own decision. He had a briefcase in his hand and seemed to fight with himself over whether to use it. He smashed Ospreay in the head after some deliberation. Still, Moxley couldn’t secure the victory.

Ospreay’s heart took over. He pulled the elbow pad off his right arm and nailed Moxley with one final Hidden Blade. He pinned Moxley, picking up the win in his first title defense.

Ospreay and Moxley shook hands after their fight. It appeared that Ospreay’s rivalry with The Death Riders had come to a close. Who steps up next was anyone’s guess, but Ospreay appeared to make that decision for everyone.

Will Ospreay shakes Jon Moxley's hand at AEW All Out on Sept. 26, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

In the post-event media scrum, Ospreay said he wanted Kazuchika Okada to challenge him for the title. Okada seemingly accepted. The match will take place at Grand Slam France on Oct. 6.

articles.title: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
articles.excerpt:
Prisoner releases and free elections were two key pledges made to the US by the new administration

Venezuelan authorities have released a slew of political prisoners, human rights groups say, days af...
articles.body_text:
Prisoner releases and free elections were two key pledges made to the US by the new administration

Venezuelan authorities have released a slew of political prisoners, human rights groups say, days after the nation's interim leader met US President Donald Trump in New York.

Among those released in the early hours of Saturday morning was Wilder Vasquez, who was handed a five-year sentence in 2018 over claims he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro.

Opposition figures have renewed calls for free elections after interim President Delcy Rodriguez held talks with Trump, who captured Maduro earlier this year, at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.

Her administration previously released hundreds of prisoners as part of a reconciliation effort following Maduro's seizure.

However, these releases slowed to a trickle in April after Rodriguez said the scheme was "coming to an end".

Venezuela's government has not made any statement concerning the latest releases, nor has it indicated whether they were the result of her conversation with the US president.

Gonzalo Himiob, vice-president of rights group Foro Penal, said "a significant number" of political prisoners had been released on Saturday morning from several of Venezuela's detention centres.

Rights groups critical as Venezuela prisoner release scheme 'coming to an end'

US lifts sanctions on Venezuelan interim leader Delcy Rodríguez

Venezuelan prison director sacked as inmates allege mistreatment

Foro Penal confirmed the release of Miguel Castillo Cedeño, who it said had been arbitrarily detained since June 2019.

Also released was Frank Cabañas, who rights groups say had been held in prison for nine years after being linked to the death of a police officer. Foro Penal said he was the only suspect who remained detained, despite family members reporting that he was suffering health problems last year.

Opposition and human rights groups have said Maduro's government used the detention of political prisoners to stamp out dissent and silence critics for years.

Rodriguez has sought to frame her interim government as more permissive of political dissent while currying favour with the US. The prisoner release scheme was a key concession by her administration to the US.

However, her decision to end the scheme attracted criticism from opposition and rights groups. Foro Penal said it was stopped with less than half of the nation's political prisoners released.

Rodriguez's government continues to deny dissidents are jailed. It has cast the release of prisoners as a gesture of goodwill and reconciliation.

Delcy Rodríguez's meeting with Donald Trump in New York has brought renewed calls for elections in Venezuela

Venezuelan Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, a minister closely associated with Maduro's authoritarian rule, called the interim president's meeting with Trump "a great triumph of the diplomacy of peace".

But opposition voices expressed their disapproval over the meeting, viewing it as a snub of their calls – that the US has previously endorsed – for swift elections.

Pedro Mario Burelli, a former Venezuelan state oil company executive and opposition commentator, called the two world leaders "the shameless puppet and her unscrupulous and undignified puppet-master", adding: "Little has changed in Venezuela under Washington's clumsy and selective oversight."

Venezuela's last elections, held in 2024, in which Maduro was declared the winner, were widely disputed as rigged. Opposition tallies suggested their candidate, who stood after Machado was barred from running, had won by 70% of the vote.

Despite this, the Trump administration backed Rodriguez, Maduro's former vice-president, as his successor rather than opposition leader María Corina Machado after Maduro was seized and put on trial on drug charges in January.

Analysts at the time cast this decision as the US choosing short-term stability in Venezuela until elections could be held.

Rodriguez used her UN General Assembly speech on Thursday to reiterate that there "will be elections in Venezuela", without specifying when.
