articles.title: Florida plastic surgeon found guilty of murdering attorney who vanished from bloody office
articles.excerpt:
Tomasz Kosowski, the plastic surgeon accused of murdering Pinellas County attorney Steven Cozzi, represents himself in his trial. (FOX 13 Tampa)

A Florida judge has found a plastic surgeon guilty of ...
articles.body_text:
Tomasz Kosowski, the plastic surgeon accused of murdering Pinellas County attorney Steven Cozzi, represents himself in his trial. (FOX 13 Tampa)

A Florida judge has found a plastic surgeon guilty of killing an attorney he’d faced in a dispute over payments for medical procedures.

The body of Steven Cozzi was never found. But prosecutors presented six days of testimony with dozens of witnesses that painted gruesome images of violent revenge.

Dr. Tomasz Kosowski, 47, represented himself in the case. He waived his right to a jury trial and, instead, put his fate in the hands of Judge Joseph Bulone.

FLORIDA PLASTIC SURGEON ACCUSED OF KILLING ATTORNEY IN HIS OFFICE DEFENDS HIMSELF IN MURDER TRIAL

The trial began on Sept. 14, more than three years since Cozzi disappeared. On Wednesday, Bulone found Kosowski guilty of killing of Cozzi.

Kosowski, clad in an orange jail jumpsuit, showed almost no reaction.

He now faces the possibility of life in prison without the chance of parole or the death penalty.

On Wednesday, Bulone reminded Kosowski there were "disadvantages" in representing himself in court. He asked if Kosowski would like an attorney for the penalty phase of the trial.

WATCH: Florida plastic surgeon asks for courtroom demonstration in murder trial

"Question No. 1: You still want to represent yourself?" Bulone questioned.

Kosowski answered without delay: "Yes, Your Honor."

"Question No. 2: Do you still want to go non-jury?" Bulone asked.

It was not immediately clear when Bulone would hand down Kosowski’s sentence.

Before resting their case, prosecutors said evidence showed that Kosowski had become obsessed with Cozzi. Angry about a years-long lawsuit, the doctor had threatened Cozzi in a restroom and stalked him outside his home, prosecutors said.

Steven Cozzi vanished in Florida. Tomasz Kosowski was charged with his murder. (Largos Police Department)

Cozzi’s husband testified that he’d been alarmed by the interactions. He’d suggested arranging for security if the two were to meet in person again.

In March 2023, Cozzi and Kosowski arranged to meet in a teleconference. A little before the scheduled meeting, Kosowski secretly slipped into the law firm, attacked Cozzi in a restroom and hauled him outside unnoticed in a wagon covered with a blanket, prosecutors said.

Kosowski showed up late for the meeting. Cozzi didn’t show up, at all.

Then they found a bathroom in the building spattered with blood. Investigators later found that the blood was Cozzi’s.

Attorney Steven Cozzi was killed in his Florida law office, authorities say. (St. Petersburg Bar Association)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Surveillance video, pieced together later using Flock cameras, showed a man pulling a wagon from the law firm, struggling to load its contents into the bed, and traveling to Kosowski’s multi-million-dollar, Tarpon Springs home.

There, prosecutors said, Kosowski transferred Cozzi to another vehicle and headed south toward the Everglades. DNA evidence found later in the garage was a match for Cozzi.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Kosowski eventually made a stop in a remote area of Florida at a dumpster, pings from his cellphone showed. There, he hoisted Cozzi into the trash container and left, prosecutors and witnesses said.

The contents were hauled to a local landfill and soon were buried under thousands of tons of garbage. Though they felt certain of Cozzi’s location and combed through trash for days, searchers couldn’t recover a body.

Police arrested Kosowski in March 2023, and he’s been held in jail ever since.

Tomasz Kosowski was accused of killing Steven Cozzi. (Pinellas County Sheriffs Office)

Throughout the trial, Kosowski sat quietly, watching witnesses and prosecutors with a bland expression. Rarely, he cross-examined witnesses.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

He called into question evidence related to DNA evidence, cellphone pings, and whether he’d really had the time and physical strength to complete the crime in the way prosecutors had testified.

The trial wrapped up for the week on Friday and resumed on Tuesday.

In his closing arguments on Wednesday, Kosowski spoke calmly and confidently.

"Not only is it impossible, physically, to do what the state asserts is required of anybody—let alone me—it makes no sense in time," Kosowski told the judge.

He gave reasons why he said he was innocent. Then, the judge paused the proceedings.

When the trial reconvened less than 30 minutes later, a statement was read aloud declaring that Bulone had found Kosowski guilty of first-degree murder.

Fox News Digital was not able to reach Kosowski for comment.

The trial will now move to the penalty phase, in which the only two options are life without the possibility of parole or the death penalty. A Spencer hearing has been scheduled for Oct. 8, which allows a defendant to present more evidence or mitigating factors to consider before sentencing.

articles.title: Giants 'hate' their fans after how they handled Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury, Craig Carton says
articles.excerpt:
Craig Carton exposes John Harbaugh and the Giants for withholding the news that franchisw QB Jaxson Dart is out the season

New York Giants fans are reeling on Wednesday, as quarterback Jaxson Dart’s ...
articles.body_text:
Craig Carton exposes John Harbaugh and the Giants for withholding the news that franchisw QB Jaxson Dart is out the season

New York Giants fans are reeling on Wednesday, as quarterback Jaxson Dart’s season has been officially ended after needing surgery to repair multiple ligaments in his left knee after a brutal hit in Monday night’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

While fans think about what the rest of the 2026 season will look like, OutKick host Craig Carton believes that it is "effectively and tangibly" at an end before their Week 3 contest against the Tennessee Titans, but he wanted to bring up a different issue when analyzing this all.

Carton believes the Giants hate their fan base – and Dart’s injury is proof of that in his eyes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants walks off the field after a play against the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) (Harry How/Getty Images)

"The Giants hate you because they’re protecting information like it’s, I don’t know, what’s a good comparison? They’re protecting information like it’s McCarthyism back in the day. That’s a leap, I know it’s a leap. But follow the bouncing ball. "

The bouncing ball for Carton begins with what ESPN’s Laura Rutledge reported during the "Monday Night Football" broadcast, where the Rams defeated the Giants, 28-6, following Dart’s injury just seven plays into the game. Rutledge spoke with Giants GM Joe Schoen, who noted that Dart would be fine.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"The Giants hate you because they’re protecting information like it’s, I don’t know, what’s a good comparison? They’re protecting information like it’s McCarthyism back in the day. That’s a leap, I know it’s a leap. But follow the bouncing ball. "

The bouncing ball for Carton begins with what ESPN’s Laura Rutledge reported during the "Monday Night Football" broadcast, where the Rams defeated the Giants, 28-6, following Dart’s injury just seven plays into the game. Rutledge spoke with Giants GM Joe Schoen, who noted that Dart would be fine.

"Joe Schoen, the general manager of the New York Giants, essentially tells a national football audience that he’s fine. Jaxson Dart is fine. He might not come into this game, but the injury is nothing for Giants fans to be worried about," Carton said. "OK, great. Fast forward, we hear after the game, we’re thinking three-to-five weeks, maybe four-to-six weeks, and that it’s a sprain of the MCL. That’s good news. That means that Jaxson didn’t tear the ACL, there’s no meniscus tear, and it’s a injury he can come back from and still play football this year. Then, we look at the Giants’ schedule and theoretically, the next couple of weeks not that bad.

"But here’s the hubris of this particular Giants regime and it’s led by the capo himself, and that is Johnny Harbaugh. This is not a Mara thing. I don’t even think it’s a Schoen thing as incompetent as Joe Schoen is and as wrong as he was about the injury update during the broadcast, and man oh man, he could not have been more wrong. He screwed the pooch on that one."

When Giants fans, and the rest of football fans, found out that Dart’s injury was actually much more serious, Giants head coach John Harbaugh had just addressed the situation during his Tuesday press conference. He said he wanted to wait on further evaluations and wasn’t clear about what Dart was dealing with.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart shakes hands with Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford after an NFL game in Inglewood, Calif., on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. (AP Photo/Caroline Brehman)

Remember, this came after the initial belief that Dart would miss time with an MCL sprain, but it wouldn’t be for the entire season.

Then, after Harbaugh’s press conference, NFL insiders began reporting that Dart is facing a much more serious injury and that losing him for the season was on the table.

"John Harbaugh decided that you, as a long-suffering Giants fan, the people that pay $100 to park at MetLife Stadium, the people that drop thousands and thousands of dollars on tickets and on the product, which has sucked, for the last decade, he decides to play Stalin with you. He decides you don’t deserve information," Carton added. "That’s a slap in the face to Giants fans when the report is out there. And the report only comes from one or two places. Let’s play this out for a second, OK? When the insiders get a report, it either comes from directly a team source, A, or it comes from directly the players or their representatives, B. There’s no C, there’s no D.

"When the information is now public that the injury is now worse than initially thought, and the Giants were the people that told the national audience and Giants fan base at halftime it’s not that bad, and that by proxy means you’ve given the fan base bad information and far more positive than the reality of the situation, why would you leave the fan base with bad information? Why not just, at that press conference, that took place within an hour of the report coming out that the injury to Jaxson Dart was far more serious, why not acknowledge it?"

Carton added: "You’d think that after a decade of losing and all the promise this year, the least the Giants could do is be straight with their fan base."

It’s a bleak outlook for Giants fans moving forward this season, and it hurts even more considering the hype that followed Week 1’s victory over the Dallas Cowboys. It felt that the Harbaugh era, led by Dart at quarterback, was on to bigger and better things than the second-worst record in the NFL over the last decade.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart walks off the field with an injury during the first half of an NFL game against the Los Angeles Rams in Inglewood, Calif., on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. (AP Photo/Caroline Brehman)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

And while the Giants could still string together wins, especially with easier opponents in "toss-up games" over the next few weeks, Carton doesn’t want the fan base to have any false hope.

"Don’t get it twisted: the New York Giants’ season is over," he said.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: ‘Ukraine did not choose this war’, Volodymyr Zelenskyy tells UN general assembly - live
articles.excerpt:
Ukrainian president reminds delegates of scale and impact of war in Ukraine during his appearance, claiming that Putin will come for other cities after Donetsk

Zelenskyy is using his appearance at th...
articles.body_text:
Ukrainian president reminds delegates of scale and impact of war in Ukraine during his appearance, claiming that Putin will come for other cities after Donetsk

Zelenskyy is using his appearance at the UN General Assembly to remind delegates of the scale and impact of the war on Ukraine, claiming that even a partial victory would not be enough for Vladimir Putin.

Putin will claim Donetsk isn’t enough for him, and will come for other Ukrainian cities, Zelenskyy says.

“Russia has used over 2,100 missiles against us. More than 950 of them were ballistic missiles.”

“They launch jet-powered Shahed [missiles] every hour… We are fighting them 24/7”.

He says this is “to make life harder for the economy and to disrupt our lives. They disrupt children at school. Would your country survive something like this?”

“Ukraine did not choose this war,” Zelensky adds.

Namibian president Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah joined growing calls for a woman to be elected as the next United Nations secretary-general.

Addressing member nations, Nandi-Ndaitwah noted that no woman has held the position since the organisation was established in 1945, and said the UN’s leadership should reflect the gender equality it promotes across the international system.

“Namibia therefore, believes that it is time that a woman is elected as secretary-general of our Organisation,” she said.

Earlier, Panama’s president, José Raúl Mulino, also called for for the Latin America and Caribbean region to have a permanent seat on the UN security council.

double quotation markI wish to reiterate before this general assembly the need for Latin America and the Caribbean to hold positions with greater decision-making power on the security council, specifically a permanent position, as a permanent member of this organization’s security council.

We are a leading region in food, minerals, biodiversity, and [have] a deep commitment to peace and integration.

He urged the UN to address urgent issues including migration and the climate crisis, adding:

double quotation markWe must acknowledge that citizens do not believe these kinds of gatherings benefit them. Herein lies one of the reasons why trust must be restored.

Our conclusion is unequivocal: the world does not need less United Nations; it needs a United Nations that works better.

Polish president Karol Nawrocki spoke of the grave importance of accountability if there is to be lasting peace and “if international law is to be anything other than a declaration without any real power”.

The absence of accountability in the international community has “sent a signal [to aggressive states] that violations of international law, aggression, and imperialist policies could go unpunished,” he told member nations.

double quotation markIt is precisely this lack of justice - this sort of original sin of the postwar order - that creates space for the return of old aggressive ambitions and methods of operation.

He went on: “Russia is destablising the situation in Europe through open aggression, hybrid operations, acts of subversion and sabotage, and by ignoring successive resolutions of this assembly.”

double quotation markContempt for international law must not become the norm.

As a country that neighbours Russia, he said he wanted to make it clear on behalf of Poland that “we are not the ones seeking confrontation”.

double quotation markWe are strengthening our alliances, developing our military, and modernizing its equipment not to wage war, but to prevent it … Our goal is deterrence and defence.

Nato remains the “guarantor of transatlantic security”, he said.

“Russia is carrying out actions aimed at undermining the foundations of international stability,” Nawrocki went on.

double quotation markIf aggression is not met with an adequate response, it becomes an invitation to repeat it.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev ⁠is heading to the United States on ⁠Wednesday, where ⁠he ​will meet with Trump administration representatives Steve Witkoff, ⁠Jared Kushner and others, two sources familiar with ⁠preparations for the talks ​have told Reuters.

The ‌sources said ‌that Dmitriev’s visit to ‌the US, which was agreed upon with Vladimir Putin, will take place in New York on ‌the sidelines of the UN general ​assembly and will follow up on a meeting between Putin ⁠and US representatives at the ​Kremlin earlier ​this month.

One ​source told Reuters that ​the ‌aim of ​the ​visit is to keep the Russia-US dialogue and the peace-making effort going.

President of Panama José Raúl Mulino is now up. He kicks off by applauding multiculturalism and the role of the UN in a world of “such volatility”, but calls for greater leadership.

“We must restore trust,” he says, warning that illegal people trafficking was taking a heavy toll on the country socially and economically, but also on some sensitive natural environments in Panama.

“We must make headway together on the key issues,” he says. This includes world trade, with Panama’s canal playing a key global role, but he warns it is increasingly at risk from heavy rain and flooding which is worsening due to the climate crisis, despite Panama being a carbon negative country.

President of the Central African Republic, Faustin-Archange Touadéra, is now on the podium, speaking about the country’s ongoing sectarian conflict and political instability.

“A fragile country needs security for development,” he says, calling for international support. “Peace cannot be decreed, it must be built day after day through dialogue, justice and shared development.”

“Holding out your hand to yesterday’s opponent is not a sign of weakness”, he says.

He also warns about the worsening impacts due to the global climate crisis and calls for a greater role for women in public life to help end instability in the country.

Zelenskyy ends by describing Russia’s continued war as “madness”, urging global action to secure peace.

“Please, everyone here, don’t be the last to join those who defend life. Be the first to say ‘we guarantee security’. Thank you to everyone who helps and everyone who stands with us – with our people, with our children.”

Zelenskyy urges leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues and impede its war efforts, telling the UN General Assembly that “Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he says.

Zelenskyy warns that continued Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy system would result in retaliation in kind.

“Ukrainians understand that this winter could be very hard for us. But in response we will have no choice but to make it painful for Russia too.”

Zelenskyy is using his appearance at the UN General Assembly to remind delegates of the scale and impact of the war on Ukraine, claiming that even a partial victory would not be enough for Vladimir Putin.

Putin will claim Donetsk isn’t enough for him, and will come for other Ukrainian cities, Zelenskyy says.

“Russia has used over 2,100 missiles against us. More than 950 of them were ballistic missiles.”

“They launch jet-powered Shahed [missiles] every hour… We are fighting them 24/7”.

He says this is “to make life harder for the economy and to disrupt our lives. They disrupt children at school. Would your country survive something like this?”

“Ukraine did not choose this war,” Zelensky adds.

A reminder that Zelenskyy’s speech comes after he met with Donald Trump on the sidelines of the gathering in New York yesterday, after the US president insisted he was working with both sides to end the war, despite little evidence of Vladimir Putin being open to any settlement.

“It’s going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand,” Trump said in his UN speech.

But Washington has since held separate talks with Moscow - and today said it had invited Putin to the G20 summit in Miami later this year.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is speaking now. We’ll bring you all the key lines here.

Israel’s ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, reasserted Israel’s claim to the occupied Golan Heights, in response to Syria’s interm president Ahmed al-Sharaa’s address to member nations earlier.

“But no speech will change reality, al-Jolani: the Golan Heights will always be part of Israel,” Danon wrote on X, using the nom de guerre al-Sharaa went by when he was HTS leader.

Al-Sharaa harshly criticized Israel’s occupation of southern Syria and said the Golan Heights is an inseparable part of his country.

In his speech, he said that Israel has carried out more than 500 air and artillery strikes on Syria since he took power nearly two years ago. Israel has also carried out 1,200 land incursions and detained nearly 300 people, he said.

He also repeatedly invoked UN security council resolution 497, adopted in 1981, which declared Israel’s annexation of the Golan Heights “null and void and without international legal effect”.

Most of the Golan Heights plateau has been occupied by Israel since 1967. It was fully annexed in 1981, a move not recognised by most of the international community.

Nikos Christodoulides, president of the Republic of Cyprus, told member nations:

double quotation markThe international order is not simply changing. It is being tested in an unprecedented way.

But it is in such times of uncertainty that the fundamental values ​​of multilateralism must be protected:

International law. The charter of the United Nations. Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. The peaceful resolution of disputes. Respect for human rights. The equality of states.

In these rapidly changing times, he said, “the credibility of the UN must be preserved. And credibility requires consistency in the application of international law.”

Christodoulides said that 52 years since the illegal Turkish invasion of Cyprus:

More than a third of the territory of the Republic of Cyprus remains under Turkish occupation

Tens of thousands of displaced people and their descendants have been prevented from returning to their homes

Varosha has remained sealed off, with Turkey still defying its clear and specific obligations set out in the relevant UN security council resolutions

And “we have been experiencing violations of fundamental human rights, the destruction of religious and cultural heritage, and the organized transfer of settlers that constitutes demographic alteration”

“Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity are not rhetorical figures,” he said. “Nor should they be applied selectively, depending on who the perpetrator is.”

double quotation markUN Resolutions cannot be applied in one case and ignored in another.

And the sovereignty and territorial integrity of a state cannot depend on its size, its strength, or the passage of time.

This is not just an issue that concerns Cyprus.

It concerns the credibility of the international system itself.

Christodoulides said he listened carefully to Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s speech yesterday in which he spoke of international law, and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states, the illegal occupation, the refugees (in relation to Israel and Palestine).

“However, in relation to Cyprus, Turkey is doing the exact opposite. Maximum hypocrisy,” Christodoulides said.

double quotation markMr Erdoğan, if you wish to invoke the charter, you must first implement it.

I remain fully committed to achieving a comprehensive solution.

I am ready to resume negotiations from where they were interrupted in 2017, building on the substantial work that has already been accomplished, within the agreed United Nations framework.

He called on Erdoğan “to allow meaningful negotiations within the framework agreed upon by the UN” to find a solution “that will allow Greek Cypriots, Turkish Cypriots, Maronites, Armenians and Latins to live together in peace, security and prosperity.”

double quotation markFor my part, let me repeat, I am absolutely committed.

Because partition will not be accepted. This cannot and will not be the future of my homeland and my people. Never. Our determination to reunite our island is unwavering.

Iran’s president said his country’s people had been the “victims of terrorism” by the United States. Delivering a rare wartime speech at the UN General Assembly, Pezeshkian displayed images of the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei and more than 150 schoolchildren killed in the opening days of the conflict.

“We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists,” Pezeshkian said at the General Assembly. “Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed upon our country. And we defended ourselves with utmost strength. America and Israel attacked us.”

On the strait of Hormuz, Pezeshkian said: “We cannot let some have free access and gain their interest from a waterway, while at the same time using that waterway to impose their aggressions upon us, to impose insecurity upon us, to forbid us access to our own waterways.” He also warns that any “expansion of warfare will not result in security.”

Argentine president Javier Milei attacked the UN in a speech to the world body, calling it a “useless organization” filled with “arrogant parasites.” The firebrand Milei, one of US president Donald Trump’s closest Latin American allies, has repeatedly used the UN platform to criticise global governance and its “woke” agenda.

Milei accused the United Nations of having failed in its duty to guarantee collective security and human rights, saying it had instead allowed “chaos, violence and international terrorism” to flourish. The UN, he said, “has become a useless organization, serving only to feed a caste of fatally arrogant parasites disguised as well-intentioned bureaucrats.”

The United States has invited Russian president Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders being held in Miami in December, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said. “In order to solve problems, you have to meet with the people that you disagree with or the people that you might have some issues with, so we’ve invited president Putin to the G20.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio said after meeting with Russia’s Sergei Lavrov that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ‌ceasefire involving grain and ​energy. “We would be open to playing a constructive role in making that happen,” he said, quoted by Reuters.

Paraguay’s president Santiago Pena called for Venezuela’s reintegration into the South ⁠American trade bloc Mercosur, speaking to world leaders at the UN General Assembly earlier today. Venezuela has been indefinitely suspended as a member ⁠of Mercosur, which comprises some ⁠of South ​America’s biggest economies, including Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.

Syria’s interim president harshly criticized Israel’s occupation of southern Syria and said the Golan Heights is an inseparable part of his country. In a speech to the UN General Assembly, Ahmad al-Sharaa said that Israel has carried out more than 500 air and artillery strikes on the country since he took power nearly two years ago. Israel has also carried out 1,200 land incursions and detained nearly 300 people, he said.

The Kremlin has responded to Andy Burnham’s speech at the UN general assembly, accusing the UK prime minister of “stoking anti-Russian sentiment”. Burnham told the UN yesterday that his government would set up a new national centre to tackle information attacks by foreign powers and singled out Russia over what he described as the spread of disinformation.

The United States has invited Russian president Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders being held in Miami in December, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said.

“In order to solve problems, you have to meet with the people that you disagree with or the people that you might have some issues with, so we’ve invited president Putin to the G20.

“We think it’s an opportunity for him to engage not just with the president but with other world leaders. We hope that’s an invitation he’ll accept,” Rubio said.

articles.title: Rockies make brutal MLB history not seen in 60 years as moribund season wraps up
articles.excerpt:

The Colorado Rockies could lose every game for the rest of the season and still finish 14 games better than last ...
articles.body_text:
Other teams could do what the Dodgers do, they simply choose to remain uncompetitive.

The Colorado Rockies could lose every game for the rest of the season and still finish 14 games better than last season. The bad news? If that happens, they will finish with 105 losses.

On Tuesday, the Rockies clinched their fourth straight season with 100 or more losses with their 7-2 defeat against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Coors Field. They are the first team since the expansion New York Mets from 1962-65 to achieve the dubious feat and just the fifth to do it overall.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

So while they will improve by at least 14 games, and maybe more if they finish strong, the season will go down in the books as another disappointing one. First-year manager Warren Schaeffer said the team has to learn from the experience.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Colorado Rockies starting pitcher Kyle Freeland hands the ball to manager Warren Schaeffer as he is pulled from the mound in the fourth inning of a game against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski)

"You learn your hardest lessons in difficulty in life," said Warren Schaeffer, in his first season as Colorado’s full-time manager.

"This is not easy. Last year, we talked about it at the end of the year, how we want to feel this and never feel it again and remember it and hold on to it. The guys have done that. We’ve just lost 100 again. There are a ton of lessons to learn from it. If we don’t learn these lessons from these games this year, we won’t get better."

The moribund Rockies have struggled mightily for over a decade and a half now. They have made the postseason just twice since 2010, and have not won a postseason series since reaching the World Series in 2007.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Colorado Rockies left fielder Zac Veen catches a fly ball off the bat of Arizona Diamondbacks' Ildemaro Vargas as shortstop Cole Carrigg looks on in the eighth inning of a baseball game Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski)

The Rockies' pitching staff has once again been a major problem, as their team ERA of 5.57 is the highest in baseball. Colorado has finished with the highest team ERA every season since 2022, and if it does so again this year, it will become only the third club since 1913 to have the worst ERA in the majors in five consecutive seasons.

Despite the rough season, the Rockies have a couple of promising pieces for the future.

Rookie first baseman TJ Rumfield entered Tuesday fifth in the National League with a .300 batting average and led all qualified rookies in batting average and on-base percentage. Hunter Goodman, Colorado’s 26-year-old catcher, was an All-Star for a second consecutive season and is one home run shy of becoming the first Rockies player with 40 homers in a season since 2019.

Colorado Rockies' Mickey Moniak heads up the first-base line after connecting for a solo home run off Colorado Rockies starting pitcher Kyle Freeland in the third inning Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski)

Veteran pitcher Kyle Freeland, who has been with the team for 10 seasons, said the team is heading in the right direction.

"I think everything we’re doing inside this clubhouse — coaches, players, front office, all staff — has been doing an incredible job to make sure that this team and this org is heading in the direction that is winning," Freeland said. "You see it."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: ‘Miracle on the Hudson’ hero Sully Sullenberger reveals Alzheimer’s warning signs he missed years ago
articles.excerpt: Dr. Jeremy Koppel discusses a new blood test's potential to predict Alzheimer's disease risk by identifying abnormal tau protein. He emphasizes its current use for diagnosing symptomatic individuals r...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Jeremy Koppel discusses a new blood test's potential to predict Alzheimer's disease risk by identifying abnormal tau protein. He emphasizes its current use for diagnosing symptomatic individuals rather than predicting future onset in healthy adults, highlighting ongoing research advancements.

Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger, the former airline pilot celebrated worldwide for safely landing US Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River in 2009, is taking on a new mission to raise awareness about the early signs of Alzheimer’s disease.

Sullenberger, who was diagnosed with the disease in August 2025, spoke on "Good Morning America" alongside his wife, Lorrie, to share their personal experience with the condition.

The couple revealed several subtle shifts in routine and behavior that began surfacing several years before he received an official medical evaluation.

'MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON' HERO CAPTAIN 'SULLY' SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER'S DIAGNOSIS

Reflecting on the timeline leading up to her husband's formal assessment, Lorrie Sullenberger noted that small adjustments in everyday life slowly pointed toward a bigger shift.

Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger (left), the former airline pilot celebrated worldwide for safely landing US Airways Flight 1549 (right) on the Hudson River in 2009, is taking on a new mission to raise awareness about the early signs of Alzheimer’s disease. (Getty; AP Photo/Steven Day)

"A lot of what I think people see in the news are late-stage Alzheimer's symptoms. And so in the very beginning, they are so subtle. And my advice to someone would be, it's what's unusual for your person," she shared, emphasizing how early symptoms often manifest gradually rather than abruptly.

TV NEWS ANCHORMAN REVEALS HE HAS ALZHEIMER'S DURING FINAL NIGHT HELMING BROADCAST

Public understanding of Alzheimer’s disease frequently focuses on these late-stage symptoms, such as pronounced memory loss, severe disorientation or difficulty managing basic daily routines. However, medical experts say early-stage cognitive decline can be much harder to spot.

"One of the first things I noticed was that it was harder and harder to remember people’s names, even people we knew," Sullenberger said. "That’s still an issue. Just forgetting things that I normally wouldn’t. Or repeating myself, not realizing that I just said that an hour ago."

Capt. Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger was diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's disease in August 2025 and is advocating for prompt testing at the first sign of cognitive changes. (Chip Somodevilla/Reuters)

Early indicators of Alzheimer's often present as mild cognitive impairment or subtle changes tailored to an individual’s normal baseline, according to health resources like Cleveland Clinic.

These can include misplacing everyday items, mild difficulty finding the right words during conversations, subtle changes in mood or executive function, or taking slightly longer to complete familiar tasks.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Because these early shifts often mimic normal signs of aging, loved ones are usually the first to notice small anomalies in behavior.

"I’ve gone through harder things than this before," Sullenberger said in the interview.

Lorrie Sullenberger emphasized that the key to spotting early cognitive decline is identifying changes that are "unusual for your person," rather than waiting for obvious late-stage symptoms. (Dave Kotinsky/FilmMagic)

The former pilot may be best known for successfully performing the "Miracle on the Hudson" in January 2009.

After US Airways Flight 1549 suffered a dual engine failure following a bird strike shortly after taking off from New York's LaGuardia Airport, Sullenberger drew on decades of flight experience to glide the Airbus A320 onto the frigid Hudson River, where all 155 passengers and crew survived, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The emergency landing made Sullenberger an internationally recognized public figure and became known as the "Miracle on the Hudson."

Lorrie Sullenberger noted that family members should trust their instincts when something feels off, advising that the key lies in identifying "what's unusual for your person."

"I’ve gone through harder things than this before."

The Sullenbergers stressed that acknowledging potential early symptoms and seeking evaluation can profoundly impact a patient’s journey. While there is no cure for Alzheimer’s, early detection allows individuals and families to explore emerging treatment options, join clinical trials, adopt lifestyle modifications and plan for the future.

"An early diagnosis is so critically important," Sullenberger said. "If you have doubts, get tested. Because the sooner you act, the more options there are, the better the outcome is likely to be."

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.title: Mitch McConnell swarmed by security as reporter pleads: 'Can you say a word for us?'
articles.excerpt: Sen. Mitch McConnell remained silent as reporters shouted questions about his health and wife Elaine Chao while security and aides surrounded the Kentucky Republican in Washington, D.C. (Credit: Sophi...
articles.body_text:
Sen. Mitch McConnell remained silent as reporters shouted questions about his health and wife Elaine Chao while security and aides surrounded the Kentucky Republican in Washington, D.C. (Credit: Sophia Leone/Fox News)

Sen. Mitch McConnell remained silent as reporters peppered him with questions about his health and his wife’s response to his hospitalization during a striking scene in Washington, D.C., on Wednesday.

"How’s it going, Mitch? Can we get a thumbs up?" one reporter called as security and aides surrounded the 84-year-old Kentucky Republican.

"Were you upset that Elaine didn’t promptly return to see you in the hospital, sir?" another asked, referring to McConnell’s wife, former Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao.

MCCONNELL'S WIFE, ELAINE CHAO, SAW NO NEED FOR 'IMMEDIATE RETURN' FROM CHINA AS FORMER GOP LEADER HOSPITALIZED

Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., walks at the Senate Subway heading to a vote on the ninth day of a partial shutdown of the federal government at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, on Oct. 9, 2025. (Kent Nishimura/Reuters)

"Senator, how are you feeling today?" a reporter repeatedly called. "Can you say a word for us, sir?"

McConnell did not answer as the group moved past the cameras.

KENTUCKY GOVERNOR CALLS ON MCCONNELL TO PROVE HE IS FIT TO SERVE OR RESIGN: 'ADDRESS THE PEOPLE'

Sen. Mitch McConnell is helped up steps as he enters the US Capitol in Washington, DC on February 2, 2026. (ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP via Getty Images)

The striking scene comes amid ongoing questions about McConnell’s health after a series of falls and public freezing episodes in recent years.

McConnell returned to Capitol Hill last week after a roughly three-month absence following a June fall that briefly knocked him unconscious. He later said he was also treated for mild pneumonia.

The longtime Kentucky senator stepped down as Senate Republican leader at the beginning of 2025 and announced weeks later that he would not seek reelection. His current term ends in January 2027.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.
